takeaway: Bile salts are reabsorbed mainly in the terminal ileum and return to the liver: the enterohepatic circulation.

question.text: Bile salt reuptake principally occurs where?
question.say: Where does bile salt reuptake principally occur?

answer.say: The answer is in the ileum.

lines.text: The ileum welcomes the travellers home.
lines.say: The happy ileum opens its arms. This is where bile salts are taken back up.

lines.text: 90 to 95% of bile salts are reabsorbed.
lines.say: Between ninety and ninety-five per cent of bile salts are absorbed from the small intestine, mostly from the terminal ileum.
(laugh) They ride their wagon along the golden road of the enterohepatic circulation.
Back at the liver, they are excreted again into bile.

lines.text: The pool recycles 6-8 times a day.
lines.say: The whole pool recycles twice per meal, about six to eight times a day.

lines.text: Remember: bile salt reuptake happens in the ileum.
lines.say: Remember: bile salt reuptake happens in the ileum, mainly the terminal ileum.
